title: Choose the smallest tree lifetime that satisfies the algorithm
description: Select a workload, processing mode, document size, and concurrency. The model exposes its memory assumptions so you can reason about tree retention before replacing them with measurements from representative files.

workloads.label: Configuration bundle
workloads.detail: A bounded document is queried repeatedly across distant branches before a transformed document is emitted.
workloads.accessReason: The transformation joins values across distant branches and revisits nodes. A one-pass record stream would need a separate state model or an intermediate representation.

workloads.label: Inventory feed
workloads.detail: Each item is validated and written independently; completed item subtrees do not need to remain resident.
workloads.accessReason: Each item is a self-contained record, so end-event processing can emit it and clear its subtree.

workloads.label: Event archive
workloads.detail: A large append-style export is reduced record by record into counters and a compact output stream.
workloads.accessReason: The reduction keeps aggregate state rather than old elements, so processed records can be cleared.

modes.label: Retain the full tree
modes.detail: Use parse() or fromstring() when the algorithm needs arbitrary navigation, document-wide XPath, mutation, or full-document serialization.

modes.label: Process end events and clear
modes.detail: Use iterparse() when records can be completed independently, then clear processed elements and preceding siblings.
